entry.title: Best Website Builders in 2026 (Ranked & Reviewed)
entry.content:
I’ve built websites on every major platform. Here’s my honest ranking based on actually using them — not reading marketing pages.

Quick Comparison

Rank Tool Best For Free Tier Starting Price Rating
1 Wix Beginners, small businesses Yes $17/mo 4.5/5
2 Squarespace Creative portfolios No (14-day trial) $16/mo 4.4/5
3 WordPress Blogs, complex sites Yes (.com) $4/mo (.com) 4.3/5
4 Webflow Designers, agencies Yes $14/mo 4.2/5
5 Shopify E-commerce No (14-day trial) $29/mo 4.4/5
6 Carrd One-page sites Yes $9/year 4.0/5

1. Wix — Best Overall

Why it’s #1: Wix offers the best combination of ease of use, features, and value. The 800+ templates mean you’ll find something that fits your industry, and the drag-and-drop editor is the most intuitive available.

Best for: Small businesses, freelancers, restaurants, portfolios, blogs

Pros: Free plan, 800+ templates, easiest editor, app market, built-in SEO tools

Cons: Can’t switch templates after publishing, free plan has branding, site speed can vary

Wix full review →

2. Squarespace — Best for Design

Squarespace templates are the most polished in the industry. If design quality matters more than template variety, Squarespace is the choice.

Best for: Creative portfolios, photographers, designers, artists

Pros: Beautiful templates, clean code, faster loading, better blogging

Cons: No free plan, fewer templates, slightly harder to learn

Wix vs Squarespace comparison →

3. WordPress — Most Flexible

WordPress powers 40%+ of the web. It’s the most flexible option but requires more technical knowledge — you’ll manage hosting, updates, and security yourself.

Best for: Blogs, complex sites, advanced SEO, custom functionality

Pros: Unlimited flexibility, 50,000+ plugins, best SEO, largest community

Cons: Steep learning curve, requires maintenance, hosting costs extra

4. Webflow — Best for Designers

Webflow gives designers pixel-perfect control without writing code. It’s more powerful than Wix but harder to learn.

Best for: Designers, agencies, marketing sites, portfolios

Pros: Pixel-perfect control, clean code export, built-in CMS, animations

Cons: Steeper learning curve, no free plan on custom domains, more expensive

5. Shopify — Best for E-commerce

If you’re building an online store, Shopify is the specialist. It handles products, payments, shipping, and inventory better than any general-purpose builder.

Best for: Online stores, dropshipping, e-commerce businesses

Pros: Best e-commerce features, 6,000+ apps, payment processing, shipping

Cons: More expensive ($29/mo+), transaction fees on non-Shopify payments, not for non-store sites

6. Carrd — Best for Simple Sites

Carrd builds beautiful one-page sites for $9/year. If you just need a landing page, link-in-bio, or simple portfolio, Carrd is the cheapest option.

Best for: Landing pages, link-in-bio sites, simple portfolios

Pros: Incredibly cheap ($9/year), beautiful templates, fast setup

Cons: One-page only, no blogging, limited functionality

How to Choose

Your Situation Best Choice
First website, want it easy Wix
Creative portfolio Squarespace
Blog with lots of content WordPress
Need design control Webflow
Online store Shopify
Simple landing page Carrd

For most people, start with Wix. The free plan lets you test, and upgrading is straightforward when you’re ready.

Our Top Pick: Wix

The easiest way to build a professional website. Start free.

Try Wix Free

FAQ

What is the best website builder in 2026?

Wix is our top pick for most users. It offers 800+ templates, a free plan, and the easiest drag-and-drop editor. For creative portfolios, Squarespace has more polished designs. For maximum flexibility, WordPress.

Can I build a website for free?

Yes, Wix and WordPress.com both have free plans. Free plans include platform branding and subdomains. Paid plans ($12-30/month) remove branding and add custom domains.

Which website builder is best for SEO?

WordPress is the best for SEO with plugins like Yoast and Rank Math. Wix and Squarespace have good built-in SEO tools. For most small businesses, any of these platforms handle SEO adequately.

Should I use WordPress or a website builder?

Use a website builder (Wix, Squarespace) if you want simplicity and don’t want to manage hosting, updates, or security. Use WordPress if you need maximum flexibility, advanced SEO, or complex functionality.

How much does a website cost in 2026?

With a website builder: $0-30/month for most sites. With WordPress: $5-30/month for hosting plus domain ($12/year). Custom development: $3,000-$50,000+. Website builders are the cheapest option for simple sites.

entry.title: Wix vs Squarespace 2026: Which Website Builder Should You Choose?

link.title: Wix vs Squarespace 2026: Which Website Builder Should You Choose?

entry.content:
Wix and Squarespace are the two biggest website builders. I’ve used both for client projects — here’s how they actually compare.

Quick Verdict

  Wix Squarespace
Best for Beginners, small businesses Creative portfolios, aesthetics
Ease of use Easier Slightly harder
Templates 800+ 100+ (more polished)
Free plan Yes No (14-day trial)
Starting price $17/mo $16/mo
Our rating 4.5/5 4.4/5

Choose Wix for flexibility and ease of use. Choose Squarespace for design quality and creative portfolios.

Feature Comparison

Feature Wix Squarespace
Drag-and-drop editor Yes (free-form) Yes (structured)
Templates 800+ 100+
Free plan Yes No
Custom domain Paid plans Paid plans
E-commerce Business plans Business plans
Blogging Basic Better
SEO tools Good Good
App market Yes (250+) Limited extensions
Mobile editing Yes Yes
Code injection Yes Yes
Member areas Yes Yes

Ease of Use

Wix

Wix’s editor is free-form — you can drag elements anywhere on the page. This gives you freedom but can lead to inconsistent layouts if you’re not careful.

The ADI (Artificial Design Intelligence) feature can auto-generate a site based on your answers. It’s a good starting point for absolute beginners.

Squarespace

Squarespace uses a structured editor — elements snap to a grid. This keeps your design clean and consistent but gives you less freedom.

The editor is slightly harder to learn but produces more professional results by default.

Templates

Wix: 800+ Templates

Wix has one of the largest template libraries. Templates are organized by industry — restaurants, portfolios, stores, services, and more.

Downside: Once you choose a template and publish, you can’t switch. Choose carefully.

Squarespace: 100+ Templates

Squarespace has fewer templates but they’re more polished. Every template looks professional out of the box.

Upside: You can switch templates after publishing (on the old version — check current policy).

E-commerce

Both platforms offer e-commerce on business plans:

  Wix Squarespace
Starting plan Business ($36/mo) Business ($33/mo)
Transaction fee 0% 3% on Business plan
Payment gateways Multiple Stripe, PayPal
Abandoned cart Yes Yes (higher plans)
Inventory management Yes Yes
Shipping labels Yes Yes

For serious e-commerce, both work. Squarespace has cleaner product pages; Wix has more e-commerce features.

Blogging

Squarespace wins for blogging. Its blog layouts are more refined, the editor is better for long-form content, and the category/tag system is more flexible.

Wix blogging is functional but basic. If blogging is central to your site, Squarespace is the better choice.

SEO

Both platforms have improved their SEO tools significantly:

  Wix Squarespace
Meta tags Customizable Customizable
URL structure Clean Clean
Sitemap Auto-generated Auto-generated
301 redirects Yes Yes
Structured data Yes Yes
Page speed Can be slow Generally faster

For most small business SEO needs, both are adequate. Squarespace tends to produce faster-loading sites.

Pricing

  Wix Squarespace
Free plan Yes No
Personal $17/mo $16/mo
Business $29/mo $23/mo
E-commerce $36/mo $33/mo
Advanced $159/mo $65/mo

Prices are similar. Wix’s free plan is a significant advantage if you want to test before committing.

When to Choose Wix

  • You want a free plan to test
  • You need maximum template variety
  • You’re a beginner who wants simplicity
  • You need an app market for extra features
  • You want drag-and-drop freedom

When to Choose Squarespace

  • Design quality is your top priority
  • You’re building a creative portfolio
  • Blogging is central to your site
  • You want cleaner, faster-loading pages
  • You prefer structured, consistent layouts

Try Wix Free

Start building your website with Wix's free plan. No credit card required.

Try Wix Free

FAQ

Is Wix better than Squarespace?

Wix is easier to use and has more templates. Squarespace has more polished designs and better for creative portfolios. Neither is objectively better — it depends on your priorities.

Which is cheaper, Wix or Squarespace?

Wix has a free plan (Squarespace doesn’t). Paid plans are similar: Wix starts at $17/mo, Squarespace at $16/mo. For e-commerce, both charge around $27-33/mo.

Can I switch from Wix to Squarespace?

There’s no direct migration. You’d rebuild your site on the new platform. Content can be exported/imported in some cases, but design and structure need to be recreated.

Which has better templates, Wix or Squarespace?

Wix has more templates (800+ vs 100+). Squarespace templates are more polished and cohesive. If you want quantity and variety, choose Wix. If you want refined design quality, choose Squarespace.

Is Squarespace better for portfolios?

Yes, Squarespace is generally better for creative portfolios. Its templates are designed with photographers, designers, and artists in mind. The layouts are more gallery-focused and visually refined.

Bubble is the most capable no-code builder. It handles complex workflows, multi-user apps, and marketplace platforms that other tools can’t.

Pros: 5,000+ plugins, large community, handles complex workflows, mature platform

  2. What’s my technical level? Beginner → Base44 or Glide. Intermediate → Bubble.
  3. Do I need app store distribution? Yes → Adalo. No → Base44 or Bubble.
  4. What’s my budget? Tight → Base44 (free tier). Flexible → Bubble or Softr.

For most people reading this, start with Base44. It’s the fastest way to go from idea to working app, and the free tier lets you validate before you pay.

Our Top Pick: Base44

The fastest way to build a web app without code. Start free.

Try Base44 Free

What is the best no-code app builder in 2026?

Base44 is our top pick for most users. It offers AI-assisted development, a generous free tier, and the fastest path from idea to working app. For complex applications, Bubble is more powerful but harder to learn.

Can I really build an app without coding?

Yes. No-code platforms handle the backend, database, authentication, and hosting. You build visually by dragging components and connecting data. I’ve built and shipped 5 real apps without writing code.

How much does it cost to build an app without code?

Most platforms have free tiers. Paid plans range from $14-$99/month depending on features. Compare that to $15,000-$50,000 for a custom-coded MVP. No-code is 10-100x cheaper for validating ideas.

Are no-code apps good enough for production?

For startups validating ideas, internal tools, and apps with under 10,000 users — yes. For high-scale consumer apps, you’ll eventually need custom code. No-code is best for MVPs and early-stage products.

Base44 and Glide are the easiest to learn. Base44 has an AI assistant that builds features from plain English descriptions. Glide turns Google Sheets into apps. Both take hours to learn, not weeks.

entry.title: I Built an AI Tutor App with Base44 — And It Uses the Socratic Method

link.title: I Built an AI Tutor App with Base44 — And It Uses the Socratic Method

entry.content:
Why Build an AI Tutor?

Most tutoring apps just give you the answer. That’s not how learning works. The Socratic method — asking guiding questions instead of providing answers — has been proven to help students understand concepts deeper and retain information longer.

I wanted to build an app that uses this approach, powered by AI. And I wanted to build it without writing a single line of code.

What I Built

Thinkerwell — a personalized AI tutoring app that:

  • Uses the Socratic method to guide students to answers through questions
  • Adapts to each student’s grade level and preferred learning style
  • Tracks streaks, progress, and mastery across subjects
  • Supports multiple subjects: math, science, history, programming, and more
  • Includes a courses dashboard where students can browse and track their learning path

The Owl Mascot

The app features a friendly robot owl mascot — a wise tutor character that guides students through their learning journey. The owl appears on the home page, onboarding flow, and quiz sessions, giving the app a warm, approachable feel.

How the Socratic Method Works in the App

Instead of saying “The answer is 42,” the tutor asks:

  1. “What do you already know about this problem?” — Gets the student thinking
  2. “What would happen if we tried X?” — Guides exploration
  3. “Can you see a pattern here?” — Helps discover the solution
  4. “Why do you think that works?” — Reinforces understanding

The student arrives at the answer themselves — which means they actually understand it.

How Base44 Made It Easy

I built this entire app in under 4 hours using Base44. Here’s the process:

Step 1: Described the app. I told Base44: “Build a personalized AI tutoring app using the Socratic method. Include onboarding where students pick their subject and level, a courses dashboard, a quiz page that asks guiding questions instead of giving answers, and a learning hub with streak tracking.”

Step 2: Base44 generated the full stack. Within an hour, Base44 created:

  • The onboarding flow with subject selection
  • The courses dashboard with progress tracking
  • The AI tutor chat interface (powered by Base44’s AI agent system)
  • The learning hub with streaks and badges
  • Authentication (email + Google login)
  • The database schema for sessions, messages, and student profiles

Step 3: Customized the design. I asked Base44 to use a purple gradient theme with the owl mascot, rounded corners, and smooth animations. The result looks polished and professional.

Step 4: Published with one click. The app was live on a Base44 URL immediately — no hosting setup needed.

What Base44 Handled

Feature How Base44 Did It
AI Tutor Brain Built-in AI agent with custom instructions
User Authentication Email + Google login, built-in
Database Auto-generated entities for sessions, messages, profiles
Hosting Included — app is live on a base44.app URL
SSL Security Automatic
Responsive Design Mobile-friendly out of the box

The Tech Behind It

What’s impressive is that Base44 generated a full-stack app with:

  • React frontend with routing and components
  • Managed database with entities for Students, Sessions, Messages, and Courses
  • AI agent (“Sage”) configured with Socratic teaching instructions
  • Row-level security so each student only sees their own data
  • Real-time chat for the tutoring sessions

All of this from a single text prompt. No code. No configuration files. No DevOps.

Why This Matters

Whether you’re:

  • A teacher wanting to create personalized learning tools
  • An edtech founder wanting to prototype an idea fast
  • A parent wanting to build a study helper for your kids
  • An entrepreneur wanting to replace expensive tutoring SaaS
